facts.subject: emergency access
facts.text: Use of emergency access shall generate prominent audit events and shall require post-event review by the Data Governance Steward and the responsible operational authority.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: During Contingency Fallback State, access control shall continue to enforce role separation even when some integrations are unavailable and manual coordination becomes necessary.

facts.subject: Regional Flow Platform
facts.text: When normal connectivity is restored, the Regional Flow Platform shall reconcile contingency actions with the Collaborative Decision Log so that accountability is preserved across the full incident timeline.

facts.label: reconcile contingency actions with the Collaborative Decision Log

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: After connectivity is restored, audit processing shall treat reconciled contingency actions as part of the same operational record as actions taken during Normal Operations.

facts.subject: Regional Flow Platform
facts.text: The Regional Flow Platform shall record slot compliance events in the Audit Event Ledger using the operating date, flight identifier, airport, runway direction, and applicable regulation reference.

facts.label: record slot compliance events in the Audit Event Ledger using the operating date, flight identifier, airport, runway direction, and applicable regulation reference

facts.subject: compliance assessment
facts.text: Each compliance assessment shall compare the Calculated Takeoff Time, the Target Off Block Time, actual off-block time, and actual takeoff time against the tolerance defined in the Business Rules Registry.

facts.subject: Slot Compliance State
facts.text: The Slot Compliance State shall indicate whether a flight was compliant, early, late, exempted, substituted, cancelled, or pending review at the end of the traffic period.

facts.subject: Audit Event Ledger
facts.text: The Audit Event Ledger shall preserve the time source applied by the Time Synchronization Service so that later review can distinguish operational delay from data latency.

facts.label: preserve the time source applied by the Time Synchronization Service

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: User decisions entered through the Airport CDM Portal shall be linked to the authenticated role provided by the Identity Access Service.

facts.subject: Collaborative Decision Log
facts.text: The Collaborative Decision Log shall retain the stated reason, decision time, affected flight, and visible operational context for each material change to a slot or sequence.

facts.label: retain the stated reason, decision time, affected flight, and visible operational context for each material change to a slot or sequence
uses the permission email to justify an approved slot substitution during post-operations review

facts.subject: substitution records
facts.text: Substitution records shall show the original flight, replacement flight, assigned Calculated Takeoff Time, acceptance status, and any subsequent cancellation or reversion.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: When an Aircraft Operator Representative proposes a substitution, the audit trail shall capture whether the change preserved the constraints of the active Ground Delay Program.

facts.subject: Slot Coordinator
facts.text: The Slot Coordinator shall review substitution activity after operations to confirm that priority rules were applied consistently across participating operators.

facts.label: review substitution activity after operations to confirm that priority rules were applied consistently across participating operators

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Late operational changes shall be distinguished from planned updates by comparing the change timestamp with the freeze horizon held in the Business Rules Registry.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Changes made inside the freeze horizon shall require a reason code and shall be visible to the Regional Flow Manager during post-operations review.

facts.subject: Tower Sequence Manager
facts.text: The Tower Sequence Manager and Ramp Movement Board shall provide actual movement milestones that support independent verification of slot performance.

facts.label: provide actual movement milestones that support independent verification of slot performance
provide actual movement milestones that support independent verification of slot performance

facts.subject: Surface Surveillance Adapter
facts.text: Surface movement evidence from the Surface Surveillance Adapter shall be retained long enough to support dispute resolution and regulatory audit requests.

facts.subject: Capacity Assessment Module
facts.text: Capacity changes made through the Capacity Assessment Module shall be correlated with the active Airport Capacity Plan and Airport Acceptance Rate used at the time of allocation.

facts.subject: Performance Analytics Warehouse
facts.text: The Performance Analytics Warehouse shall aggregate compliance outcomes by carrier, route group, regulation, airport operating configuration, and time band.

facts.label: aggregate compliance outcomes by carrier, route group, regulation, airport operating configuration, and time band

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Aggregated metrics shall support review of systemic lateness without exposing commercially sensitive detail beyond authorized roles.

facts.subject: Data Governance Steward
facts.text: The Data Governance Steward shall verify that audit fields required for slot performance reporting remain complete, immutable, and traceable to approved data definitions.

facts.label: verify that audit fields required for slot performance reporting remain complete, immutable, and traceable to approved data definitions

facts.subject: System Support Engineer
facts.text: The System Support Engineer shall investigate technical gaps when audit sequences show missing events, duplicate updates, or inconsistent timestamps.

facts.label: investigate technical gaps

facts.subject: Regional Flow Manager
facts.text: The Regional Flow Manager shall use the Post Operations Report to identify whether noncompliance resulted from operator choice, airport constraint, airspace constraint, weather impact, or system issue.

facts.label: use the Post Operations Report to identify whether noncompliance resulted from operator choice, airport constraint, airspace constraint, weather impact, or system issue

facts.subject: Airport Duty Manager
facts.text: The Airport Duty Manager shall review late airport-driven changes that affected multiple flights and shall record whether the operational justification was valid.

facts.label: review late airport-driven changes that affected multiple flights
record whether the operational justification was valid

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Findings from the review shall feed adjustments to tolerance values, reason code definitions, and training material, subject to change control.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: All audit outputs shall be retained according to the approved records schedule and shall remain searchable for compliance investigations, performance meetings, and lessons-learned activity.

facts.subject: Regional Flow Platform
facts.text: Data governance for the Regional Flow Platform shall assign accountable owners to each operational data domain and shall make those assignments visible in the Airport CDM Portal.

facts.subject: Data Governance Steward
facts.text: The Data Governance Steward shall maintain the data ownership register and shall coordinate updates through the Business Rules Registry.

facts.label: maintain the data ownership register
coordinate updates through the Business Rules Registry

facts.subject: Regional Flow Manager
facts.text: The Regional Flow Manager shall own flow management policy data, including Ground Delay Program parameters and Tactical Regulation Proposal status values.

facts.subject: Slot Coordinator
facts.text: The Slot Coordinator shall own slot allocation reference data, including Calculated Takeoff Time tolerances and Slot Compliance State definitions.

facts.subject: Airport Duty Manager
facts.text: The Airport Duty Manager shall own airport capacity declarations, including Airport Capacity Plan records and Airport Acceptance Rate values.

facts.subject: Tower Supervisor
facts.text: The Tower Supervisor shall own tower sequence status data maintained for the Tower Sequence Manager.

facts.subject: Ramp Control Lead
facts.text: The Ramp Control Lead shall own ramp movement status data maintained for the Ramp Movement Board.

facts.subject: Meteorology Briefing Officer
facts.text: The Meteorology Briefing Officer shall own operational weather classification inputs accepted by the Weather Ingest Gateway.

facts.subject: Airline Operations Coordinator
facts.text: The Airline Operations Coordinator shall be accountable for airline-supplied schedule intent, readiness status, and Target Off Block Time updates submitted through approved interfaces.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Each owned data element shall have a defined business meaning, allowed value range, update authority, retention class, and escalation contact.

facts.subject: freshness indicator
facts.text: Freshness indicators shall be displayed on the Common Situation Display wherever stale data could affect sequencing, metering, regulation, or resource allocation decisions.

facts.label: displayed on the Common Situation Display

facts.subject: freshness indicator
facts.text: The freshness indicator shall include the time of last accepted update, the maximum permitted age, and a visual state that distinguishes current, aging, stale, and unavailable data.

facts.label: current
aging
stale
unavailable

facts.subject: Time Synchronization Service
facts.text: The Time Synchronization Service shall provide the common time basis used for freshness calculations across the Regional Flow Platform.

facts.label: provide the common time basis used for freshness calculations across the Regional Flow Platform

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The Demand Prediction Service, Capacity Assessment Module, Slot Allocation Engine, and Departure Metering Service shall reject data that lacks a trusted timestamp.

facts.label: reject data that lacks a trusted timestamp
reject data that lacks a trusted timestamp
reject data that lacks a trusted timestamp
reject data that lacks a trusted timestamp

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Validation rules shall include schema checks, mandatory field checks, code set checks, temporal sequence checks, and operational plausibility checks.

facts.subject: Flight Data Exchange
facts.text: The Flight Data Exchange shall validate Flight Intent Message content before the data is made available for operational use.

facts.label: validate Flight Intent Message content

facts.subject: Surface Surveillance Adapter
facts.text: The Surface Surveillance Adapter shall apply position quality checks and shall mark uncertain observations before they are used by surface decision functions.

facts.label: apply position quality checks
mark uncertain observations

facts.subject: Airline Interface Adapter
facts.text: The Airline Interface Adapter shall apply carrier-specific format checks while preserving the common operational meaning required by the Regional Flow Platform.

facts.label: apply carrier-specific format checks

facts.subject: Handling Resource Planner
facts.text: The Handling Resource Planner shall validate resource quantities, task timing, and allocation identifiers against active operational reference data.

facts.label: validate resource quantities, task timing, and allocation identifiers against active operational reference data

facts.subject: Business Rules Registry
facts.text: The Business Rules Registry shall hold the current validation thresholds, allowable reason codes, and exception rules approved for Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, and Contingency Fallback State.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: When a discrepancy is detected, the affected component shall mark the data as disputed and shall preserve the prior accepted value until an authorized correction is available.

facts.subject: Data Governance Steward
facts.text: The Data Governance Steward shall coordinate discrepancy resolution with the responsible operational owner and shall record the disposition in the Audit Event Ledger.

facts.label: coordinate discrepancy resolution with the responsible operational owner
record the disposition in the Audit Event Ledger

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Urgent discrepancies that could change a metering, arrival regulation, or slot allocation decision shall be raised through the Alert Distribution Hub and reviewed in the Digital Briefing Room.

facts.subject: System Support Engineer
facts.text: The System Support Engineer shall investigate technical causes of missing, delayed, duplicated, or transformed records and shall provide evidence needed for stewardship decisions.

facts.label: investigate technical causes of missing, delayed, duplicated, or transformed records
provide evidence needed for stewardship decisions

facts.subject: Performance Analytics Warehouse
facts.text: The Performance Analytics Warehouse shall retain data quality measures, including validation failure rates, freshness breaches, manual corrections, and recurring ownership conflicts.

facts.label: retain data quality measures, including validation failure rates, freshness breaches, manual corrections, and recurring ownership conflicts

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Stewardship reviews shall use those measures to update training, adjust validation rules, and improve the reliability of information used in operational decision making.

facts.subject: Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System
facts.text: Performance measurement for the Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System shall convert operational events into repeatable indicators that can be reviewed after each operating day.

facts.subject: Performance Analytics Warehouse
facts.text: The Performance Analytics Warehouse shall calculate delay absorption as the portion of expected airborne or terminal-area delay that is converted into controlled ground delay before departure.

facts.label: calculate delay absorption as the portion of expected airborne or terminal-area delay that is converted into controlled ground delay before departure

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Delay absorption shall be measured by comparing the unconstrained demand predicted by the Demand Prediction Service with the regulated demand produced by the Slot Allocation Engine and the realized movement times captured through the Flight Data Exchange.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The principal delay absorption indicator shall report minutes absorbed at origin, minutes remaining in the arrival stream, and minutes transferred to surface queues within the region.

facts.subject: Regional Flow Manager
facts.text: The Regional Flow Manager shall use this indicator to verify that a Ground Delay Program reduced airborne holding without creating excessive departure congestion at constrained airports.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Queue length performance shall be measured for runway departure queues, arrival metering queues, apron movement queues, and regulation waiting lists.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The Tower Sequence Manager shall provide runway sequence counts, while the Ramp Movement Board shall provide surface queue counts based on movement status and surveillance confirmation.

facts.label: provide runway sequence counts
provide surface queue counts based on movement status and surveillance confirmation

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The North Runway Meter, South Runway Meter, East Apron Sensor, and West Apron Sensor shall support independent checks of queue length where surveillance coverage is available.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Queue metrics shall include maximum queue length, average queue length, time above threshold, and recovery time after a constraint is lifted.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Slot adherence shall be measured as the difference between actual movement times and the assigned Calculated Takeoff Time or Target Off Block Time.

facts.subject: Slot Coordinator
facts.text: The Slot Coordinator shall review slot adherence by operator, airport, time band, and regulation identifier to detect recurring causes of noncompliance.

facts.label: review slot adherence by operator, airport, time band, and regulation identifier to detect recurring causes of noncompliance

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: A flight shall be counted within tolerance when the actual takeoff or off-block event occurs inside the operating window defined in the Business Rules Registry.

facts.subject: Slot Compliance State
facts.text: The Slot Compliance State shall be used to identify periods when adherence monitoring has operational priority over advisory optimization.

facts.label: uses the Passenger Misconnect Count to weight departure sequencing decisions when connection protection is an approved local objective

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Cancellation avoidance shall be estimated by comparing actual cancellations with a baseline scenario derived from demand, capacity, weather, and historical disruption outcomes.

facts.subject: Capacity Assessment Module
facts.text: The Capacity Assessment Module shall record the available Airport Acceptance Rate used in each baseline so that avoided cancellation estimates remain traceable.

facts.label: record the available Airport Acceptance Rate used in each baseline

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The Airline Operations Coordinator and Aircraft Operator Representative shall be able to challenge cancellation avoidance results through the Collaborative Decision Log when local business decisions affected the outcome.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Emissions reduction shall be estimated from reduced airborne holding, reduced taxi-out time, avoided engine running in queues, and smoother departure metering.

facts.subject: Performance Analytics Warehouse
facts.text: The Performance Analytics Warehouse shall apply approved fuel burn and emissions factors by aircraft category, operating phase, and delay location.

facts.label: apply approved fuel burn and emissions factors by aircraft category, operating phase, and delay location

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Emissions metrics shall distinguish between actual reductions and delay transfers that only move fuel burn from one phase of flight to another.

facts.subject: Meteorology Briefing Officer
facts.text: The Meteorology Briefing Officer shall support interpretation of emissions results by identifying periods when weather routing or convective avoidance dominated fuel performance.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Stakeholder benefit tracking shall allocate measured outcomes to aircraft operators, airport operations, air navigation service functions, ground handling activities, and passengers where the source data supports that attribution.

facts.subject: Airport Duty Manager
facts.text: The Airport Duty Manager shall receive benefit summaries that show changes in stand occupancy, surface congestion, recovery duration, and passenger-facing disruption indicators.

facts.subject: Data Governance Steward
facts.text: The Data Governance Steward shall ensure that published performance measures identify data sources, calculation versions, confidence limits, and known exclusions.

facts.subject: Post Operations Report
facts.text: The Post Operations Report shall present regional benefits alongside operational trade-offs so that decision makers can see whether delay, queue, slot, cancellation, and emissions objectives were balanced in practice.

facts.label: present regional benefits alongside operational trade-offs

facts.subject: Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System
facts.text: Training for the Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System shall be role based and shall cover normal coordination, constrained operations, recovery actions, and degraded system use.

facts.subject: Regional Flow Manager
facts.text: The Regional Flow Manager shall receive advanced instruction on interpreting demand and capacity information, leading collaborative decisions, and authorizing operational measures in the Regional Flow Platform.

facts.subject: Air traffic controllers
facts.text: Air traffic controllers shall be trained to understand how flow measures, sequencing changes, and calculated times affect sector workload, runway demand, and controller tactical flexibility.

facts.subject: Tower Supervisor
facts.text: The Tower Supervisor shall receive practical training on the Tower Sequence Manager, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, North Runway Meter, and South Runway Meter.

facts.subject: Ramp personnel
facts.text: Ramp personnel shall be trained under the direction of the Ramp Control Lead to use the Ramp Movement Board without substituting system indications for required visual checks, radio coordination, and local safety procedures.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The Airline Operations Coordinator and Aircraft Operator Representative shall be trained to submit, review, and update Flight Intent Message data through approved interfaces and to assess the operational effect of Calculated Takeoff Time and Target Off Block Time changes.

facts.subject: Ground handling personnel
facts.text: Ground handling personnel shall be trained by the Ground Handling Dispatcher on the Handling Resource Planner and on procedures for confirming that resource constraints are represented accurately before they influence collaborative decisions.

facts.subject: Slot Coordinator
facts.text: The Slot Coordinator shall receive training on the Slot Allocation Engine, Airport CDM Portal, and applicable Business Rules Registry entries so that slot actions are applied consistently and transparently.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The Network Operations Liaison and Airspace Sector Planner shall be trained to coordinate regional constraints, sector load conditions, and network measures using the Sector Load Monitor and Common Situation Display.

facts.subject: Airport Duty Manager
facts.text: The Airport Duty Manager shall be trained to recognize when an Airport Capacity Plan requires revision and when the operational state should move from Normal Operations to Adverse Weather Mode or Capacity Reduction State.

facts.subject: Meteorology Briefing Officer
facts.text: The Meteorology Briefing Officer shall be trained to explain weather uncertainty in operational terms and to verify that the Weather Ingest Gateway supports the assumptions used during briefings.

facts.subject: Emergency Response Coordinator
facts.text: The Emergency Response Coordinator shall participate in recurrent training so that emergency priorities are integrated into flow management decisions without obscuring command authority or safety responsibilities.

facts.subject: Deicing Coordinator
facts.text: The Deicing Coordinator shall receive seasonal refresher training on how deicing capacity assumptions are represented in demand and departure metering tools.

facts.subject: Data Governance Steward
facts.text: The Data Governance Steward shall train operational users on data quality responsibilities, privacy expectations, and the correct interpretation of audit records in the Audit Event Ledger.

facts.label: train operational users on data quality responsibilities, privacy expectations, and the correct interpretation of audit records in the Audit Event Ledger

facts.subject: System Support Engineer
facts.text: The System Support Engineer shall train superusers on service status checks, access fault escalation, and safe use of the Contingency Operations Console during partial outages.

facts.label: train superusers on service status checks, access fault escalation, and safe use of the Contingency Operations Console during partial outages

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Initial training shall include classroom instruction, supervised workstation practice, scenario walkthroughs in the Digital Briefing Room, and observed operational shadowing before independent system use is authorized.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Recurrent training shall be required at least annually and after major changes to the Regional Flow Platform, Demand Prediction Service, Capacity Assessment Module, or Flight Data Exchange.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Simulation exercises shall use realistic traffic samples, weather constraints, surface congestion, airline schedule pressure, handling resource shortages, and recovery objectives to test coordinated decision making.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Each exercise shall include participants from tower, ramp, airline operations, handling, airport operations, network coordination, meteorology, data governance, and system support functions when those functions are relevant to the scenario.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Exercises shall cover transitions among Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, Contingency Fallback State, and Slot Compliance State.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Simulation events shall require users to compare automated recommendations with local knowledge, document significant decisions in the Collaborative Decision Log, and explain departures from system proposals.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Human factors safeguards shall include workload monitoring, clear alert prioritization, consistent terminology, confirmation steps for high impact actions, and protection against silent mode changes.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Workstation layouts shall support rapid comparison between the Common Situation Display, Airport CDM Portal, Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, and relevant advisory messages without forcing users to copy critical values manually.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Training assessments shall verify that users can identify stale data, time synchronization problems, duplicate flights, conflicting constraints, and inappropriate automation reliance before such issues affect live operations.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Post-exercise reviews shall use evidence from the Performance Analytics Warehouse and Audit Event Ledger to improve procedures, refine training materials, and confirm that human performance concerns are assigned to accountable owners.

facts.subject: Regional Flow Platform
facts.text: Deployment of the Regional Flow Platform shall proceed through phased increments that limit operational exposure while progressively adding airports, interfaces, and decision support functions.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The first increment shall establish the core operational baseline for the Regional Flow Manager, Network Operations Liaison, Data Governance Steward, and System Support Engineer in a controlled production environment.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: This baseline shall include the Identity Access Service, Time Synchronization Service, Audit Event Ledger, Performance Analytics Warehouse, and Business Rules Registry before any airport is permitted to exchange operational data.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Pilot airport selection shall favor locations with stable operational leadership, representative traffic complexity, available surface surveillance data, and demonstrated willingness to participate in joint procedure development.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The initial pilot shall include one constrained primary airport and one less constrained regional airport so that both high-demand and routine operating patterns are exercised.

facts.subject: :null
facts.expression: one constrained primary airport and one less constrained regional airport

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Each candidate airport shall provide evidence that the Airport Duty Manager, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Airline Operations Coordinator, Ground Handling Dispatcher, and Aircraft Operator Representative have named accountable implementation contacts.

facts.subject: Readiness Gate 1
facts.text: Readiness Gate 1 shall confirm that governance, security approvals, user role definitions, operating hours, and support escalation paths are documented and accepted by local stakeholders.

facts.label: confirm that governance, security approvals, user role definitions, operating hours, and support escalation paths are documented and accepted by local stakeholders

facts.subject: Readiness Gate 2
facts.text: Readiness Gate 2 shall confirm that the Flight Data Exchange, Airline Interface Adapter, Surface Surveillance Adapter, and Weather Ingest Gateway can be connected without disrupting existing airport operations.

facts.subject: Readiness Gate 3
facts.text: Readiness Gate 3 shall confirm that local procedures have been mapped to the Airport CDM Portal, Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, and Arrival Regulation Console.

facts.subject: Readiness Gate 4
facts.text: Readiness Gate 4 shall confirm that training, shadow operations, contingency procedures, and operational acceptance criteria have been completed before live collaborative decisions are made through the Regional Flow Platform.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Interface certification shall be performed separately from operational acceptance so that technical conformance defects do not become unresolved procedural issues.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Each interface shall be tested for message structure, time stamping, identity attribution, replay handling, duplicate detection, outage recovery, and rejection behavior under degraded network conditions.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The Demand Prediction Service, Capacity Assessment Module, Slot Allocation Engine, Gate Conflict Detector, Sector Load Monitor, North Runway Meter, and South Runway Meter shall be certified against agreed reference scenarios before they are used for operational recommendations.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Certification results shall be recorded in the Collaborative Decision Log when they affect operational procedures and in the Audit Event Ledger when they affect access, configuration, or transaction traceability.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Airport onboarding shall start with data discovery workshops that identify local tools, manual workarounds, unofficial spreadsheets, and locally maintained constraint registers.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The migration plan shall classify each local tool as retired, retained for read-only reference, integrated through an approved interface, or replaced by a Regional Flow Platform function.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: No local tool shall be retired until the responsible operational owner verifies that its essential decisions, timing assumptions, and audit needs are supported in the target process.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: During shadow operations, local tools shall remain the authoritative source while the Regional Flow Platform produces parallel outputs for comparison by operational users.

facts.label: produces parallel outputs for comparison by operational users

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The cutover decision shall be based on measured agreement between local practice and Regional Flow Platform outputs, user confidence, defect closure, and demonstrated recovery from simulated failures.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: After cutover, local users shall enter operational decisions through the Airport CDM Portal and shall avoid reintroducing uncontrolled parallel records that undermine common situational awareness.

facts.subject: Contingency Operations Console
facts.text: The Contingency Operations Console shall be available at each onboarded airport before reliance on the Regional Flow Platform is declared for Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, or Contingency Fallback State.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Expansion beyond the pilot airports shall occur in waves that group airports by interface maturity, traffic dependency, stakeholder readiness, and available support capacity.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Each onboarding wave shall include a stabilization period in which the System Support Engineer and Data Governance Steward monitor defect trends, data quality, access changes, and user adoption.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Full regional deployment shall be declared only after the Regional Flow Manager confirms that operational benefits, safety constraints, cyber controls, and stakeholder obligations remain stable across multiple airports and traffic conditions.

facts.subject: Regional Flow Platform
facts.text: Operational service management for the Regional Flow Platform shall begin when a deployed airport is accepted into steady state support after the regional stabilization period.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The service model shall distinguish continuous operational support from planned engineering support so that safety related traffic flow functions remain protected at all times.

facts.subject: System Support Engineer
facts.text: The System Support Engineer shall provide round the clock on call coverage for production incidents affecting the Regional Flow Platform, Airport CDM Portal, Slot Allocation Engine, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, and Alert Distribution Hub.

facts.label: provide round the clock on call coverage for production incidents affecting the Regional Flow Platform, Airport CDM Portal, Slot Allocation Engine, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, and Alert Distribution Hub

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Standard service desk coverage for access requests, reporting questions, configuration inquiries, and minor usability issues shall be available during normal regional administrative hours on business days.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: During published peak traffic periods, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, and Recovery Phase, the on call support posture shall be raised so that the System Support Engineer can join the Digital Briefing Room without delay.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Airport Duty Manager, and Network Operations Liaison shall retain operational command authority during support activity.

facts.subject: System Support Engineer
facts.text: The System Support Engineer shall advise operational supervisors on technical status, known workarounds, data integrity concerns, and recovery options, but shall not issue traffic management instructions.

facts.label: advise operational supervisors on technical status, known workarounds, data integrity concerns, and recovery options

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Incidents shall be classified by operational effect, with the highest priority assigned to loss of common situational awareness, loss of slot computation, corruption of operational timing data, or failure of alert distribution during active traffic management.

facts.subject: critical incident
facts.text: A critical incident shall be acknowledged within fifteen minutes and shall have continuous technical ownership until service is restored or an agreed operational workaround is in place.

facts.label: acknowledged within fifteen minutes

facts.subject: high priority incident
facts.text: A high priority incident that degrades a major function without stopping tactical coordination shall be acknowledged within thirty minutes and shall be reviewed with the affected operational supervisor at least hourly.

facts.label: acknowledged within thirty minutes
reviewed with the affected operational supervisor at least hourly

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Medium and low priority incidents shall be handled through the service queue, with target updates provided at intervals appropriate to their operational impact and planned resolution path.

facts.subject: System Support Engineer
facts.text: The System Support Engineer shall maintain an incident record that captures the initial symptom, affected components, operational state, timeline, mitigation actions, data corrections, and supervisor decisions.

facts.label: maintain an incident record that captures the initial symptom, affected components, operational state, timeline, mitigation actions, data corrections, and supervisor decisions

facts.subject: incident record
facts.text: Incident records shall reference the Audit Event Ledger where user actions, configuration changes, interface events, or automated decisions are relevant to the investigation.

facts.subject: Collaborative Decision Log
facts.text: The Collaborative Decision Log shall be used to preserve the operational context of major incidents when traffic management decisions are made while a technical degradation is present.

facts.trigger: the Regional Flow Platform cannot support safe collaborative operation

facts.subject: System Support Engineer
facts.text: The System Support Engineer shall verify that fallback tools, exported operational data, and restoration checkpoints are available before advising that normal technical service can resume.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Post incident review shall be required for critical incidents, repeated high priority incidents, security related events, and failures that occur during capacity constrained operations.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The review shall identify technical root cause, operational contributing factors, effectiveness of workarounds, user communication quality, and corrective actions assigned to named owners.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Planned change windows shall normally be scheduled during low demand night periods and shall be coordinated with the Regional Flow Manager, Airport Duty Manager, Tower Supervisor, and affected Aircraft Operator Representative groups before approval.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Changes that modify the Business Rules Registry, Identity Access Service, Time Synchronization Service, Flight Data Exchange, or operational metering behavior shall require additional validation in a representative test environment before production release.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Emergency changes may be applied outside the standard window when needed to restore service, protect cyber security, or prevent material operational harm, but they shall be documented and retrospectively approved.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Service level targets shall include monthly availability for critical production functions, incident response time, restoration time, data feed timeliness, and successful completion of scheduled operational reports.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Availability targets shall exclude approved maintenance windows, customer network outages outside the managed boundary, and periods when operational supervisors have directed use of contingency procedures for nontechnical reasons.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Performance against service targets shall be reviewed with the Regional Flow Manager and Data Governance Steward so that service quality, operational benefit, data quality, and user confidence are managed as a single operating obligation.

facts.subject: Regional Flow Platform
facts.text: Future enhancement of the Regional Flow Platform should be treated as an incremental extension of the operational service rather than as a replacement of the current concept.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Cross-border exchange should use standardized message structures where practical, but the Business Rules Registry should retain the local parameters needed for Meridian operations.

facts.label: retain the local parameters needed for Meridian operations

facts.subject: Flight Data Exchange
facts.text: The Flight Data Exchange should be enhanced to accept richer intent data, including improved route options, expected cruise profiles, and updated departure readiness information.

facts.label: accept richer intent data, including improved route options, expected cruise profiles, and updated departure readiness information

facts.subject: Demand Prediction Service
facts.text: The Demand Prediction Service should use this data to create more stable demand pictures across longer planning horizons while still preserving tactical responsiveness.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Trajectory prediction should also make greater use of weather features, sector configuration, runway direction, and surface movement status when estimating flight progress.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The Weather Ingest Gateway and Sector Load Monitor should provide the common inputs needed to connect airspace capacity and airport capacity in the same prediction cycle.

facts.label: provide the common inputs needed to connect airspace capacity and airport capacity in the same prediction cycle
provide the common inputs needed to connect airspace capacity and airport capacity in the same prediction cycle

facts.subject: Capacity Assessment Module
facts.text: The Capacity Assessment Module should evolve from a mainly rules-based assessment into a service that can compare planned capacity, observed throughput, and predicted constraint persistence.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Any use of learning models should be introduced with explainability requirements so that operational users can understand why a capacity or delay estimate has changed.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Advanced turnaround prediction should combine aircraft state, handling milestones, stand occupancy, crew readiness, passenger processing, and ramp congestion signals.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The Airport CDM Portal, Airline Interface Adapter, Handling Resource Planner, and Ramp Movement Board should provide the main operational inputs for this capability.

facts.subject: Target Off Block Time
facts.text: Predicted changes to Target Off Block Time should be presented with confidence levels rather than as unconditional system corrections.

facts.subject: Slot Allocation Engine
facts.text: The Slot Allocation Engine should use improved turnaround predictions to protect feasible Calculated Takeoff Time assignments and to reduce avoidable re-sequencing.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The Tower Sequence Manager and Departure Metering Service should receive only the information needed for tactical sequencing, with detailed airline operational data controlled by policy.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Machine-assisted recovery options should support the Recovery Phase by proposing coordinated actions that balance runway throughput, sector loading, stand availability, and airline priorities.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: These options should be generated by the Contingency Operations Console and reviewed through the Common Situation Display before any operational decision is applied.

facts.label: generated by the Contingency Operations Console

facts.subject: system
facts.text: The system should not automatically impose a Ground Delay Program, change an Airport Acceptance Rate, or alter a tactical measure without authorized human confirmation.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Recovery recommendations should include the operational rationale, expected benefit, key assumptions, and possible secondary effects on connected flights and surface movements.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The Collaborative Decision Log and Audit Event Ledger should record each proposed option, the user response, and the final decision so that performance can be reviewed after operations.

facts.label: record each proposed option, the user response, and the final decision
record each proposed option, the user response, and the final decision

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Regional expansion should include a repeatable onboarding pattern for new airports, airspace sectors, airlines, and handling organizations.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The Identity Access Service, Time Synchronization Service, and Performance Analytics Warehouse should be scaled early because they form shared foundations for a wider regional deployment.

facts.subject: Data Governance Steward
facts.text: Data governance should remain under the Data Governance Steward, with clear rules for retention, consent, quality thresholds, and permitted operational use.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Future releases should be validated in shadow mode before operational activation so that the Regional Flow Manager, Airline Operations Coordinator, Tower Supervisor, and Airport Duty Manager can compare recommendations with actual outcomes.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Sustained regional ATFM and A-CDM operation requires each participating organization to treat the operating picture as a shared operational asset rather than a local advisory product.

facts.subject: Common Situation Display
facts.text: The Common Situation Display is the shared baseline for time-critical coordination and should be kept consistent with the Regional Flow Platform and Airport CDM Portal.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Calculated Takeoff Time and Target Off Block Time commitments should be treated as executable operating constraints unless they are revised through the agreed coordination process.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: Ground Delay Program decisions, Tactical Regulation Proposal review, and Airport Acceptance Rate changes should be visible to affected participants before they are applied whenever operational time permits.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The Flight Data Exchange, Airline Interface Adapter, Surface Surveillance Adapter, and Weather Ingest Gateway must be operated with monitored data quality thresholds and clear fallback procedures.

facts.subject: :null
facts.text: The Slot Allocation Engine, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, Tower Sequence Manager, and Ramp Movement Board must use the approved rules recorded in the Business Rules Registry.

facts.text: The Performance Analytics Warehouse and Post Operations Report should be used to measure compliance, delay outcomes, capacity use, and the effectiveness of collaborative decisions.
